review_comments.body:
As far as I can tell, #9869 applies to tasks that have not begun executing. That behavior is preserved as non-active tasks are still immediately marked REVOKED.

An active task with `terminate=False` is not actually revoked. https://docs.celeryq.dev/en/stable/userguide/workers.html#revoke-revoking-tasks
> When a worker receives a revoke request it will skip executing the task, but it won’t terminate an already executing task unless the terminate option is set.

I don't think a documentation update is needed because this fixes a bug rather than changing the documented behavior.
Same as https://github.com/celery/celery/pull/10564#issuecomment-5594257205
Without request= here the chord bookkeeping only happens on the later discard path, which never runs on the threads pool with terminate=True. This is exactly the #10527 hang.
This skips the backend write for active tasks, which reverts #9869 behaviour that 5.6 shipped and documents. Either keep the store here or update the docs and Changelog and explain why.
and this? @phanky1
what about this? @phanky1
False alarm. The control command no longer does chord bookkeeping.

I think we deliberately allow repeated calls to the `backend.mark_as_revoked` in the first place as
https://github.com/celery/celery/blob/4c6619c50eacf707b77e05e909d9c21cab34e363/celery/worker/control.py#L247-L248
this exception handler only logs the error and does't remove the id from `worker_state.revoked`.

If we follow this suggestion, there could be a scenario where the first result backend update fails, and someone runs revoke a second time expecting the worker to call the result backend again, but that backend call gets skipped.
@phanky1

This change alters revoke semantics in a way that can affect chord bookkeeping and idempotency (control revoke vs announce revoke vs repeated control revoke). Several unit tests that previously covered these cases were removed; please add/update tests that assert (1) repeated revoke does not duplicate chord bookkeeping, and (2) control revoke + later discard/announce does not double-report the chord member to the backend.

For active requests when `terminate=False`, the request is intentionally excluded from `requests_by_id`, which forces `backend` to fall back to `state.app.backend`. That changes backend selection for tasks that override their backend: the REVOKED state may be written to the wrong backend even though the worker *does* know the request and its backend. Consider always using the request (when found) for backend selection, while still avoiding passing request context / chord bookkeeping for active tasks unless `terminate=True`.

Removing the `_revoked_in_backend` guard means `_announce_revoked` will always call `mark_as_revoked` even if the REVOKED state was already persisted earlier via the control revoke path. For chord members, this risks double-counting/incrementing chord bookkeeping (the exact regression previously protected by tests). Reintroduce an idempotency mechanism (e.g., restore a per-request flag and have control set it when it successfully stores + runs chord bookkeeping, or change control to avoid pre-storing for locally-known requests and let the announce path be the single writer).

`_revoke` no longer filters out task ids that were already in `worker_state.revoked`, so repeating the same control revoke command will call `backend.mark_as_revoked(...)` again for the same task ids. This can cause duplicate side effects (notably chord bookkeeping in some backends) and unnecessary backend load. Restore an `unrevoked_ids`/delta filter so backend writes only happen for ids newly added to the revoked set (termination can still run for the full input list).
@phanky1 need another investigation from your side :D

Could we build this lookup from all `task_ids` now that `mark_as_revoked` no longer receives the request? On a repeated revoke, `unrevoked_ids` is empty, so a still-reserved task with a custom backend is silently rerouted to `state.app.backend`, contrary to the custom-backend behavior preserved here. Since no request context is passed anymore, looking up the request again cannot repeat chord bookkeeping.
Give me a moment, I'm almost done.
I guess this needs some more investigation on your side, right?
@phanky1 can you please verify this?

This revert removes the unit tests that exercised chord-member revocation via `app.control.revoke` / `control.revoke(...)` (including the chord bookkeeping path). If the chord hang is still a known/possible regression here, it would be good to keep a minimal regression test that reproduces the hang (or asserts the chord counter/callback behavior) so we can safely iterate on an alternative fix.

`control._revoke()` now always calls `state.app.backend.mark_as_revoked(...)` for every incoming ID, even if it was already revoked, and even when the worker has a locally-known request whose task overrides `Task.backend`. This can cause unnecessary backend writes on repeated revoke commands and can write the REVOKED state to a different backend than the task uses (Request uses `self.task.backend.mark_as_revoked(...)`).
